messages:
maria.perez: heads-up — Acme just escalated: they want per-tenant quota/usage dashboards in Q2. they said it’s a blocker for their renewal.
alex.choi: ack. do we treat this as a high-impact customer ask (bump R/I) or as a pre-sales retention win (lower effort)?
jamie.k: quick thought — impact looks high for ACME specifically, but small across base. current RICE would overweight it unless we normalize by customer cohort.
sam.reed: agree with jamie. we’ve seen this before: one big customer skews impact. propose two options: 1) special case (deliver as customer success eng), 2) include as formal product initiative but use cohort-normalized impact so RICE reflects broader value.
maria.perez: product + sales asked for a single decision today. can we do a lightweight normalization rule?
alex.choi: suggestion: compute Impact_score = min(estimated_revenue_uplift / total_revenue, 0.25) to cap single-customer influence, then multiply by reach (pct of customers affected). that keeps RICE from exploding on single accounts.
jamie.k: that’s better than previous. also we should surface sequencing constraints: this depends on quota API work in eng-runtime (two-week spike). if we postpone platform work, multiple features get blocked. so effort increases if we sequence wrong.
sam.reed: putting numbers: reach=0.02 (ACME only), impact_raw=0.8 (their value). cap to 0.25 => impact=0.25. Reach*Impact = 0.005. even with medium confidence we get low RICE. that argues for customer-specific handling.
natalie: +1 on CS-led patch. we can ship a templated dashboard and a paid enablement for enterprise customers to cover cost. then product invests later if we see >5 similar asks.
maria.perez: ok can we capture that as a decision? i.e., temporary CS implementation, add to backlog with tag `prio:watch` and re-evaluate in 6 weeks.
alex.choi: logging decision: 
```
decision: CS patch for ACME; product backlog item 'tenant-usage-dashboards' with cohort-normalized RICE recalibration; re-eval in 6w
launch-criteria: >5 paying customers request OR platform quota API completed + SLOs for one week
```

jamie.k: one more ask — when we recalc RICE for the backlog, can we also adjust Confidence to account for integration complexity? last time we under-estimated because we treated infra work as simple.
sam.reed: +1. propose bumping Effort by 1.5x for infra-tied tickets when kernel/platform dependencies exist. helps sequencing decisions.
maria.perez: sounds consensus. @prod-bot can you create the backlog ticket and add label `watch-cohort` and assign to @jamie.k for estimation?
prod-bot: created ticket PROD-4827 "tenant-usage-dashboards (watch-cohort)" and assigned to jamie.k — https://redwood.example/PROD-4827 :white_check_mark:
natalie: thanks — i'll coordinate CS enablement and draft the customer SOW for ACME so they don't churn while we wait.
alex.choi: for the Q2 prioritization doc, i'll add a short appendix describing the cohort-normalized RICE rule and the infra-effort multiplier. want to avoid repeated manual overrides.
maria.perez: perfect. meeting note: temporary CS solution now, backlog watch item created, re-eval in 6 weeks or sooner if we hit >5 requests. moving this off the urgent pile for roadmap scoring. :thumbsup:
sam.reed: noting sequencing risk: if kernel quotas land late, platform multiplier makes this initiative costlier -> may flip ranking with predictive cache. keep an eye in weekly prio sync.
jamie.k: will estimate PROD-4827 tomorrow and flag any hidden infra deps.
maria.perez: thanks team. closing thread unless someone objects.
